# *Data Cleaning*

## Overview:
### Our project draws on two source files: the aggregated business/jobs file and the address-level establishment file. Each maps onto a different half of our research question, so rather than cleaning each file as an end in itself, our cleaning process is organised around producing three analysis-ready tables for the team to build on. `TO DISCUSS`

- **Table 1 — Industry & Employment Trends** (`df_small_clean`):
  `census_year x clue_small_area x industry x business_size`, with `total_establishments` and `total_jobs`. 
  This is our primary table for identifying which industry sectors and CLUE areas have experienced sustained growth or decline — the core of our research question.

- **Table 2 — Address-level Data for Maps**: (`df_large_clean`)
  The cleaned address-level file, with the ANZSIC code fix applied and location ID columns dropped, kept for anyone doing spatial visualisation with geolocations — like our heatmaps, mapping establishment density, vacancy clusters by coordinates, etc.

- **Table 3 — Vacancy/Underutilisation Data** (`vacancy_by_area_year`):
  `census_year x clue_small_area`, with `n_establishments`, `n_vacant`, and `vacancy_rate`. 
  This is our measure of business-space underutilisation, and feeds directly into the infrastructure-need/policy-planning half of our research question.


## 1. Table 1 — Industry & Employment Trends from df_small_raw

TLDR:
- No text inconsistencies found for area, industry, and business size. 

- Checked for NAs across all columns. Only total_jobs had missing vals (4,252 obs). All other columns (Census.year, CLUE.small.area, ANZSIC.indusrty, Business.size, Total.establishments) were fully complete.

- Explored Total jobs missing vals (Large business 59% missing, Medium 31%, Non employing 45%, Small business 14%). It doesn't seem like a data collection error, it could be data suppression to restrict business information. `TO DISCUSS`

- Checked for total_establishments/total_jobs == 0. 1,451 rows of total_jobs == 0 come from Non employing business size, so no data cleaning required.

```{r}
# Check NAs
colSums(is.na(df_small_raw))

# Clean names + convert census year to date
df_small_clean <- df_small_raw |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(census_year = as.Date(paste0(census_year, "-01-01")))

df_small_clean |>
  group_by(business_size) |>
  summarise(pct_na_jobs = mean(is.na(total_jobs)))

# how many rows have total_establishments == 0?
df_small_clean |> 
  filter(total_establishments == 0) |> 
  nrow()

# how many rows have total_jobs == 0, broken down by business_size?
df_small_clean |> 
  filter(total_jobs == 0) |> 
  count(business_size)

# Check text consistency on the categorical columns
n_distinct(df_small_raw$CLUE.small.area)
n_distinct(str_squish(str_to_lower(df_small_raw$CLUE.small.area)))

n_distinct(df_small_raw$ANZSIC.indusrty)
n_distinct(str_squish(str_to_lower(df_small_raw$ANZSIC.indusrty)))

n_distinct(df_small_raw$Business.size)
n_distinct(str_squish(str_to_lower(df_small_raw$Business.size)))

glimpse(df_small_clean)

# Compare number of observations (aggregated by Census year, CLUE area) in df_small vs. df_large.
df_large_summary <- df_large_raw |>
  count(census_year, clue_small_area, name = "n_from_df_large")

df_small_summary <- df_small_raw |>
  group_by(Census.year, CLUE.small.area) |>
  summarise(n_from_df_small = sum(Total.establishments), .groups = "drop")

compare <- df_large_summary |>
  left_join(df_small_summary, by = c("census_year" = "Census.year", "clue_small_area" = "CLUE.small.area"))

# Checking if df_small excludes Vacant Spaced observations
df_large_summary_no_vacant <- df_large_raw |>
  filter(industry_anzsic4_description != "Vacant Space") |>
  count(census_year, clue_small_area, name = "n_from_df_large_novacant")

```

## 2. Table 2 — Geolocational Data (Making df_large_clean)

### Steps:
### 2.1: Checking for Duplicate rows & Removing Location ID variables (block, property, base_property id) from df_large_raw. Resolving datatype issues.
### 2.2: Check & Clean Industry variables (industry_anzsic4_code and industry_anzsic4_description)
### 2.3: Check & Clean Geolocational data (longitude, latitude, and point)


## 2.1. Checking for Duplicate rows, Removing Location ID variables (block, property, base_property id) from df_large_raw, Changing census_year to datetime

TLDR:
- Duplicates: No completely duplicated rows
- We don't need it for our base analysis, we can join it back in the future if we choose to explore a "businesses per building" density feature.

```{r}
# Count duplicate rows
df_large_raw |> count(across(everything())) |> filter(n > 1)

# remove location IDs
df_large_clean <- df_large_raw |>
  select(!c(block_id, property_id, base_property_id))

# Convert census_year to a date type
df_large_clean <- df_large_clean |>
  mutate(census_year = as.Date(paste0(census_year, "-01-01")))
```

## 2.2: Check & Clean Industry variables (industry_anzsic4_code and industry_anzsic4_description)

TLDR:
- Checked for codes <-> descriptions mapping. Found no inconsistencies.
- Checked for codes that weren't 4 digits long;
  - We had 9x industry codes that were 3 digits long, they were missing a "0" in front of them. Rectified that issue
- We have 68299x business addresses that are empty (industry_anzsic4_code = 0, industry_anzsic4_description = "Vacant Space"). I chose to leave them in because we can use them to measure underutilisation.

```{r}
# Check codes that map to more than one description. 0 found.
df_large_clean |> distinct(industry_anzsic4_code, industry_anzsic4_description) |>
  count(industry_anzsic4_code) |> filter(n > 1)

# Check descriptions that map to more than one code. 0 found.
df_large_clean |> distinct(industry_anzsic4_code, industry_anzsic4_description) |>
  count(industry_anzsic4_description) |> filter(n > 1)

# Check for ANZSIC codes that aren't 4 characters long. 
# We have 68299 observations Vacant Space = 0, 
# 945 observations in 9x other 3-character industry codes.
# I checked the ANZSIC website for each of those 9 industries, I found that they are missing a "0" in front of their 3 characters. 
df_large_clean |> mutate(code_len = nchar(trimws(industry_anzsic4_code))) |> count(code_len)
df_large_clean |> filter(!grepl("^[0-9]{4}$", trimws(industry_anzsic4_code))) |> distinct(industry_anzsic4_code, industry_anzsic4_description)

# Adding a "0" to those 9x 3-character codes
df_large_clean <- df_large_clean |>
  mutate(industry_anzsic4_code = if_else(
    nchar(trimws(industry_anzsic4_code)) == 3,
    str_pad(trimws(industry_anzsic4_code), 4, side = "left", pad = "0"),
    trimws(industry_anzsic4_code)
  ))

# Check for differences in string/text formats. Same = no differences
n_distinct(df_large_clean$industry_anzsic4_description)
n_distinct(str_squish(str_to_lower(df_large_clean$industry_anzsic4_description)))
```

## 2.3: Check & Clean Geolocational data (longitude, latitude, and point)

TLDR:
- 4,785 observations (~1.2%) are missing latitude/longitude. Of these, only 1,094 (23%) are Vacant Space. The majority, 3,691 (77%), are active businesses missing coordinates, so this isn't fully explained by vacancy.

- Missingness is not evenly spread over time: it's heavily concentrated in 2016 (1,742 of 4,785, ~36%), tapering off through the mid-2010s. 2020–2024 have zero missing coordinates, so this looks like a resolved data-collection issue specific to 2016 and earlier, rather than an ongoing gap.

- Decision: Kept those rows as-is since our unit of analysis is clue_small_area, not exact coordinates. Note however that it's a known limitation for visualisation — a small subset of points, concentrated in 2016, won't plot on a map.

- Point always matched latitude/longitude when present, and was always correctly formatted. Hence its redundant, and I dropped it from df_large_clean
  
```{r}
# Checking for NA Geolocation values. We have 4785. The
df_large_clean |>
  summarise(
    na_longitude = sum(is.na(longitude)),
    na_latitude  = sum(is.na(latitude)),
    empty_point  = sum(!is.na(point) & trimws(point) == "")
  )

# Checking the other 408,765 observations' text hygiene, that its always "latitude, longitude" in string format. All in the right format
df_large_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(point), trimws(point) != "") |>
  mutate(valid_format = grepl("^-?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+,\\s*-?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$", trimws(point))) |>
  count(valid_format)

df_large_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(point), trimws(point) != "") |>
  separate(point, into = c("point_lat", "point_long"), sep = ",\\s*", convert = TRUE) |>
  mutate(lat_match  = abs(point_lat  - latitude)  < 1e-6,
         long_match = abs(point_long - longitude) < 1e-6) |>
  count(lat_match, long_match)

# Since "point" always matches to "latitude, longitude", we remove it as a variable
df_large_clean <- df_large_clean |> select(-point)

# Checking for duplicate rows after we've removed block_id, property_id, and base_property_id. There are quite alot. 
df_large_clean |> count(across(everything())) |> filter(n > 1)

# Check to see how many observations with no Geolocational data link to Vacant spaces
df_large_raw |>
  filter(is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude)) |>
  count(industry_anzsic4_description == "Vacant Space")

# Checking for missing Geolocation Data across years 
df_large_raw |>
  filter(is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude)) |>
  count(census_year) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

## 3. Table 3 — Vacancy/Underutilisation Data from df_large_clean

- Checked for rows where trading_name suggests vacancy but industry classification isn't "Vacant Space" (23 distinct code/description combos, maybe ~50 observations)

- These aren't a uniform mislabeling issue: some appear to be temporarily-closed named businesses (e.g. "Ding Dong Lounge (Currently vacant due to fire damage)"). 

- Merged into the vacancy measure regardless, since vacancy_rate is measuring active business use of space within a given census year.

```{r}
# Cross-checking vacancy classification via trading_name
df_large_clean |>
  filter(str_detect(str_to_lower(trading_name), "vacant"),
         industry_anzsic4_description != "Vacant Space") |>
  count(trading_name, industry_anzsic4_code, industry_anzsic4_description, sort = TRUE)

# Building vacancy_by_area_year
df_large_clean <- df_large_clean |>
  mutate(is_vacant = industry_anzsic4_description == "Vacant Space" |
                      str_detect(str_to_lower(trading_name), "vacant"))

vacancy_by_area_year <- df_large_clean |>
  group_by(census_year, clue_small_area) |>
  summarise(
    n_establishments = n(),
    n_vacant = sum(is_vacant),
    vacancy_rate = n_vacant / n_establishments,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
max(vacancy_by_area_year$n_establishments)
```

```{r}
vacancy_by_area_year_2020 <- vacancy_by_area_year |>
  filter(census_year == "2020-01-01") |>
  mutate(occupied = n_establishments - n_vacant) |>
  select(clue_small_area, occupied, n_vacant) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(occupied, n_vacant),
               names_to = "status",
               values_to = "count") |>
  mutate(status = recode(status, occupied = "Occupied", n_vacant = "Vacant"))

ggplot(
  vacancy_by_area_year_2020, 
  aes(x = clue_small_area,
      y = count,
      fill = status),
  ) + 
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  coord_flip() + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Occupied" = "blue", "Vacant" = "lightblue")) +
  labs(title = "Melbourne Establishments and Vacancies in 2020",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Number of Establishments",
       fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
vacancy_by_area_year_trend <- vacancy_by_area_year |>
  select(census_year, clue_small_area, vacancy_rate) |>
  group_by(clue_small_area)

# Use faceting instead of one crowded chart
ggplot(
  vacancy_by_area_year_trend,
  aes(x = census_year,
      y = vacancy_rate)
) +
geom_line(size = 1, color = "steelblue") +
facet_wrap(~ clue_small_area, scales = "free_y") +  # One facet per area
labs(title = "Melbourne Establishment Vacancy Rates across CLUE areas (2002-2024)",
     x = "Year",
     y = "Vacancy Rate (%)") +
theme_minimal() +
theme(
  strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
  plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
) +
scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1))
```

```{r}
vacancy_heatmap <- vacancy_by_area_year_trend %>%
  mutate(year = census_year)
  
ggplot(
  vacancy_heatmap, 
  aes(x = clue_small_area,
      y = year,
      fill = vacancy_rate
      ) 
) + 
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue") +
  coord_flip() + 
  labs(title = "Melbourne Establishments and Vacancies Over Time (2002-2024)",
       x = NULL,
       y = NULL,
       fill = "Vacancy Rate") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
  )
```
